title: Tech Firms, Govts. Clash For Capital: Market Snapshot
title_cn: 科技公司、政府。资本冲突：市场概况
summary:
As the AI buildout relies more heavily on credit and equity financing, access to capital is emerging as an another more acute pain point for the AI trade. Hyperscalers alongside specialized AI ventures are flooding credit markets with record amounts of new debt to pay for power-hungry data centers, chips, and energy grids. At the same time, governments, led by the US, facing skyrocketing budget deficits, rising defense budgets, and higher term premiums are issuing record volumes of sovereign debt. Traders are now making space in their portfolios for corporate bonds offering far higher yields on AI debt as a wave of potential mega-IPOs from OpenAI and Anthropic approach.

title: What the AI Industry Got Wrong About Public Backlash
title_cn: 人工智能行业在公众强烈反对方面犯了什么错误
summary:
Even those within the AI industry have been very anxious about the technology. Worries about its potential to create destabilizing job losses, or rogue AI that could lead to human extinction. But for all their anxiety, they missed the thing that's become the most publicly salient: how upset people would be about data centers. Data center construction has been happening for a long time, and it used to be relatively uncontroversial. In fact, cities and states would often design their tax code to incentivize data center construction. On this episode, we speak with independent writer and Substacker Jasmine Sun, who recently traveled to Wisconsin and Michigan to report about the communities and activists trying to stop development, what the pushback is really all about and what future developers will have to do in order to be welcomed in.

summary: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Republican Rep. Mike Lawler of New York says the US should "hold the Chinese to account" for facilitating Iran's illicit oil trade as President Donald Trump pushes an economic "D-Day" against Tehran.
